Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
i need a prompt for a handoff note from the Tuesday May 14, 2024 dinner shift at Harbor Street Community Kitchen. the shift was 3 to 8 pm and service began at 5:30, and this should be for the next shift lead, not a report about the whole kitchen program. Please get the details below into a useful order. I have a lot of scattered notes and don't want the next person to have to guess which things happened and which things still need attention. Keep the information as it is, and don't add an explanation for anything that isn't in the notes. A short opening can say what shift this covers, then a numbered section for the service and staffing details would make sense, with the remaining information in connected paragraphs. It should read like a handoff, not like a speech or a thank-you letter.

There were eight volunteers on the roster at the start. Two were new and Mara showed them the serving line and where the gloves were kept before service. One volunteer left at 6:10 because of a family call; the notes don't say who it was, so don't guess. The shift still served dinner, but I don't have a separate headcount of staff after that person left. The count on the meal sheet is 74 meals served, with six takeaway meals packed. Three meals were kept aside for late arrivals until 7:15. The notes don't say whether anyone came for those meals after that, so leave that open rather than deciding they were collected or discarded. Service began at 5:30 as planned.

The menu was lentil stew, rice, and salad. The kitchen sheet says there is no dairy in the stew. The rice was marked gluten-free, and the salad dressing contains sesame; the sesame labels were put beside the dressing bottles before serving. Don't turn that into a statement about every dish being free of an allergen. There was a question from one guest about whether the stew had dairy, and Mara checked the kitchen sheet. The guest said, “Thanks, I’ll take the rice and salad.” Don't add a name or say what else the guest ate. A small amount of salad dressing spilled near the end of service and was wiped up; it was not the same as an incident or injury.

Bread came at 12:40. The invoice listed 18 loaves and the delivery had 14, so say what the two records show without saying why they differ. I left a note about the count with the kitchen paperwork. There were also 10 unopened cans of tomatoes in the dry-store count at the end of the shift, and the shelf had two bags of rice left. Don't call either amount a shortage. The paper napkins were down to one sleeve in the serving area, while the extra napkins were still in the cabinet below the tea station. No one counted how many napkins were in that sleeve. The handoff should make the location of the extra ones clear but not claim that supplies were ordered.

The sink on the left side drained slowly during cleanup. I called the building desk at 6:35 and there had been no response by the end of the shift. Keep that as an unresolved item, not as a repair request that was accepted or completed. The refrigerator temperature was 39 degrees at 3:20 and 40 degrees at 7:50. Those are the two readings in the log; there isn't another reading between them. The evening cleaner arrived at 7:30 and wiped the tables and mopped the main aisle before the shift ended. The serving trays were washed and put on the drying rack, but the rack was still in use when we locked the kitchen at 8:00, so don't say the trays were put away.

There are three existing files in the shared folder for this shift, the meal count scan, the delivery invoice scan, and the temperature log scan. Keep their names as they are: do not rename files. You may sort the scans into the existing May 14 shift folder, which is where the three files belong. That permission is about sorting them into that folder, not changing the names. The meal count sheet is the source for 74 meals and six takeaways; the invoice and delivery count are the source for the bread difference; and the temperature log is the source for the two readings. The handoff should say these records are in the shared folder, but not claim that they were checked by anyone else.

Please leave the next shift lead with the open details that actually need following up: the slow sink and no response from the building desk, the three meals held until 7:15 with no recorded outcome, and the trays still on the drying rack at lockup. The 14-loaf delivery against an invoice for 18 is worth noting, but there is no note saying a replacement delivery was requested. The napkin sleeve and the spare napkins have locations stated above. A small amount of salad dressing spilled near the end of service and was wiped up; the notes do not describe an injury or other incident.

Bread was delivered at 12:40. The invoice lists 18 loaves and the delivery had 14. Report what each record shows without explaining the difference. A note about the count was left with the kitchen paperwork. At the end of the shift, the dry-store count showed 10 unopened cans of tomatoes and the shelf had two bags of rice left. Do not call either amount a shortage. The serving area had one sleeve of paper napkins, and extra napkins remained in the cabinet below the tea station. No one counted the napkins in the sleeve. State where the extra napkins are, but do not say that supplies were ordered.

The left-side sink drained slowly during cleanup. The building desk was called at 6:35; there had been no response by the end of the shift. Keep this unresolved and do not say that a repair request was accepted or completed. Say that these records are in the shared folder, but do not claim that anyone else checked them.

Leave the next shift lead with the recorded open details: the slow sink and the lack of a response from the building desk, the three meals held until 7:15 with no recorded outcome, and the trays that remained on the drying rack at lockup.
